sentences.text: Yeah, I saw Julie was there too.
This meeting is being recorded.
All the way back there.
Sorry about that.
No problem.
Hopefully you can hear me okay.
Yes, I can.
Where are you calling from?
I'm in New York and Julie's in Michigan.
Michigan.
And you're in the uk?
Yes, I am, yes.
Yeah, yeah, just outside London.
Do you know the UK at all?
Besides general parts of London?
No.
Okay, outside of London, but yeah, not very far away.
Okay.
But nothing's that far away from London.
So good to see you both.
Well, thank you for getting in touch.
I believe you sent an email saying roll up.
So obviously a lot to find out but happy to give you a little bit of detail about me first.
Yeah.
And just to I answered.
I mean I've been following you for a while so I just find what you have to send very interesting, which is highly unusual.
Consider I delete every email that I get and so you know roll up is.
Is an option but would love to get to know you a little more and tell you about us and hear if you have any thoughts but please go ahead.
Yes, exactly.
We can get into that.
So we are capital A, we're M and A advisory.
We just work in marketing services.
So all of our our clients are buying or selling marketing companies.

We work over at agencies Co, that's our platform for sellers and we work on the buy side as well where we tend to work with either high growth agencies or private equity, helping them to target agency businesses to acquire and help them do the entire deal as well.
And we're also involved in roll ups.
We're currently doing some rollups ourselves so hopefully you'll be a fit with one of those and I can talk you through how it works.
But very high level is that we are skipping one of the steps where most founders of agencies get taken advantage of by the financial people.
Yeah, we're basically handing those multiples back to founders and in the process hopefully adding about a third to another sort of 100% actually to, to the business, to the valuation.
So it's quite a unique way of doing it.
But it's not a.
It's not something that doesn't happen every day in M and A, but it's not something that happens in agency land very often.
So.
But anyway we would love to include you in one of those options.
What is it that you were thinking about them, Billy?
Because you did say that roll ups could be potentially an option.
But I guess it'd be good to hear more about where you are today and what the best Fit would be.
Yeah, we're kind of in a.
At a pivot point.
So we've built brand throw from the ground up for the last five years.
It came out of me serving.
I'm sorry.
I have a puppy in the background.
Can you hold?
He's only five weeks old.
He is not yet trained.
He likes attention like all babies do.
So he, the second she gets on the phone he decides he needs mommy.
My dog's like that at all times.
But she's a barker as well.
She's only tiny cockapoo.
Have you seen those?
They're like.
Oh yeah, this.
He's.
He's Shih Tzu and Maltese.
So kind of a cute little six pounder right now.
Yeah, seven pounds.
But anyway, he's just removed.
But.

So anyway, I served as a futurist for IBM when they were rolling out Watson after I wrote a book probably about 10 years ago and then I worked with them for a couple of years after and that's how I learned about AI and how, why we built Brad and throw into what it is because we got endorsement about the idea of using AI plus human emotion and data science to be able to be the only company in the world that's able to score human emotion.
So it was a solve for the failure of sentiment analysis, natural language processing, biometrics and all the other means that are used to measure emotion in the customer feedback loop.
So we've built a successful.
We have a automated platform.
It's not fully automated end to end, but we have a.
We're able to go out and basically collect data, demonstrate it on a platform and show clients it as an option for traditional research.
And a lot of people, you know, are.
We've had early adopters, many Fortune 500 companies.
It's just, we've had growth year over year.
The pandemic happened in the middle of our growth while we were building the technology with our Lighthouse client who was EY and HP that disrupted things Net Net.
We got back on track when Julie joined the company to be our chief customer officer.
She's now our chief growth officer in 2022.
And we had a very, very successful year in 2023.
We did 15 proof of concepts using the technology.
So much so that we were so bullish and we were talking to an investor who was very interested.

We decided to build out what we could do if we were to actually create scalable products that didn't necessarily require our services because originally what we built was what we thought was a software as a service.
But it turned out to be something that people wanted us to do for them.
So we've been successful over the last couple of years working on what I just mentioned.
We decided for a variety of reasons that the investor who strung us along for a year and a half was not someone that we wanted to work with for a variety of reasons.
And we're at a pivot point right now of thinking about what do we do next?
Do we wait and see what happens if the market corrects itself and raise money?
Maybe do.
But would it be potentially an easier or better path for us to go back to our roots?
We both have worked at agencies and use our technology in partnership with the right agency partner to maybe, you know, we've been offered aqua hire situations.
They weren't very appealing based off of who the partners were.
But that's kind of where we're at.
We're at a pivot of how do we get to the next level and, and what does that look like?
Because the technology is very powerful.
Together we are, you know, I want to be flattering ourselves but we worked at with some of the leading brand.
We're very seasoned, well known marketers in the industry and there's just a lot of assets here and we're not exactly sure what to do with them.
Okay, cool.
All right, so tell me a little bit more about what it is that you actually do.
I know you've kind of given me an overview, but how does that work directly with, with the clients that you have?
So it's unfortunately like a one to, it's like a one off model which is why I have my Forbes column right.

So I get a lot of leads from there and we basically take on a research project and use our methodology of scoring how people feel because we're able to de risk every type of go to market or creative strategy.
Because we're literally saying if you say X to this customer, they're going to feel why they're going to behave this way and you're either going to engender trust or you're not.
Simply because of our algorithm's ability to do that and how we built our platform.

Then because we are experts in branding and marketing, we tell them also how to action the insights as opposed to just throwing a, you know, 120 page deck at them and telling them, you know, goodbye and good luck.
Here's your research.
We've tried to pivot into the to have ongoing engagements because our belief is that research needs to now be agile so that it should be foundational research.
And then you have the ability to do sprints on top of it.
But because of everything that's going on in the economy for the last year and a half, all of the momentum that we had behind that idea unfortunately has lost a little bit of the wind in itself.
Okay, so do you actually have any AI in what you're doing or is it ended up just being a.
Oh, it's definitely, it's AI machine learning, Data science, which was proven out on Wall street to predict market movements.
That's how our head of data science actually invented the math for what we do.
We built the application, he built the math.
He was able to predict market movements using 100 data points.
We have very small sample size that are predictive of a population with near 100% accuracy.
So we're able to reach very hard to reach audiences and turn around the data within a week or two time.

You know, with hard audiences like, you know, we have a lot of B2B clients who appreciate our ability to get to the C suite and senior buyers, although we also work with luxury brands like Equinox and Moet Hennessy.
So one would think that there would be in reading your.

Your stuff and how you talk about things, there's a landscape shift taking place, as we all know, and there might be an agency partner that would be interested in using this as a differentiator as well as using us to be part of their team.
We are having some of those conversations ourselves.
But as I said, you caught my attention.

You do this for a living and it would be much, I don't know, it would be educational and beneficial to talk to somebody who knows what they're doing as opposed to Jerry rigging what we're doing through our contacts.
Although to be honest with you, we do have interest from a couple of PR firms.
Firms.
But so what?
Who cares?
I mean, that's great, but.
So where are you at the moment then, Billy?
Just in terms of the, the actual business is.
Is it just you two in that actually do the day to day work or do you have a team that works with you as well?
We do the day to day work.
We have a frat, you know, we have, we have a cap table.
So we have our fractional CTO is, you know, part time.

Our head of product is, or everyone is, is working for sweat equity besides Julie and myself at the present time, the chief experience officer for five years, who we recently let go because there, there was not, you know, he, he built the platform, he built the website.
At this time, there was no need to have him, but he's obviously one of our partners as well.
And so you took on investors as well.
VC was it?
We were about to take on investment.
That's why we, you know, we created the cap, we have the cap table, we have everything formalized.
But as I, as I mentioned, the investor who we were going to work with at the end of last year has turned out to not be anything of what he said he was going to be in Q1.
So we decided to step away from that.
And then in terms of like, you know, any revenue that's coming through the business, is that all minimal now?
You've not managed to, to get the flywheel going?
Is that, is that what's happened?
Well, we, I mean we had a very strong first quarter.
I mean we, I think we had 250k first quarter.
It's, it's not a problem this year.
Yeah.
Yeah.
Okay.
So you're probably going to hit a million this year, do you think?
Yeah, yeah.
I mean, go ahead, Julie, you can talk about our numbers.
No, I mean, yeah, I mean in 2023 we're at 1.3 million.
Last year was a little bit more difficult, is where we really focused on our products and our, how we could sort of get scalable products.
So we spen the first half of the year doing that, but still came in, I think 800.
And this year I think we're probably on track for a million, a million plus.
But I mean the environment is a little bit tumultuous, so it's hard to, to plan.
But you know, our pipeline is strong and again we have relationships with very top tier brands that often pop up, you know, and come back for a second engagement.
Do you know what your EBITDA is or your net profit at the moment?
Our net profit, you know, with all of our expenses, I think it was somewhere in the 500k range when we had a million.
But I don't, I don't have a hard time.
It depends.
We have a financial advisor and he answers the EBITDA question in different ways.
Depending on who needs to, who needs to get the information.
So I'm just thinking about what, what size business could acquire, what you'd be looking for.
So you've been talking to PR companies you said that are interested in merging with you or is that something that you're thinking about yourself?
It's, it's where we have, it's.
Listen, it's where our roots are.
I ran C suite advisory business with insights embedded in it at Weber that's where I met Julie.
She worked on the political side of the house as well as the consumer side of the house.
And we came together again after being apart for about 13 years.
As I mentioned in 2022.

We do have really good contacts and we thought we would lean into them to explore this idea of not necessarily acquiring, but maybe a joint venture or us being fractional part of their research teams.
And that is something that is potentially going to work out.
But again, we wanted to speak to you because you do this for a living and you specifically said you have a network of agencies who are looking to differentiate.
And I think we have a differentiator both in our reputation, our talent and our tech.
And maybe we could find.
You could find the right marriage.
Yeah, I think sure.
It's size as much as sort of how much they've invested in building out.
You know, is it build or buy?
Right.
So have they invested a lot in terms of internal research?
Are they open to new kinds of research?

Because basically if someone's doing traditional statistical research or even using, you know, synthetic data with traditional research, we can really come in and we're predictive and quantifiable and we're measuring emot, the only ones that do that.

So it's someone that wants to be an early adopter, is open to maybe doing things differently and wants to use sort of the landscape and the environment right now of people trying to understand how to use technology, you know, with the AI, you know, sprinkled in to differentiate the company.
And as a selling point as they go in for new business where we think we can be very helpful and both winning new business as well as helping to grow business for them with the insights.
It's all about the bottom line in terms of what we do.
Okay, and your current clients, do you have those clients in retention or do they come to you just like on a project by project basis?
How are you sort of engaging?
Mostly what we do, I mean, for a lot of them, we start with a pilot because since it is new technology, they come in with a pilot.
But we have MSAs with a lot of very big companies from PwC to Moet Hennessy to Kyndryl.
So typically we do MSAs and then we have sows that are, you know, more project based based on their different needs across the business.
So it really varies.
How much roughly are those contracts worth?
Yeah, each client, is it a range of value values across the year or do you charge like similar fees to everybody?
So it's usually based on the research and the segmentation.

And so a typical project for us might cost, if they're doing foundational benchmark research, let's say in multiple countries with C suite buyers might be anywhere from, you know, 60 to $80,000 for an engagement that also includes an executive summary, a presentation, strategic briefs, a lot of the actionable items that they can then use to actually hit the ground running as well.

And what we've pivoted to most recently, since my background is very heavily B2B and it seems that B2B marketers are finally opening up the, their minds to traditional market research being broken and leaning into emotion.
You know, we've been thinking about B2B agencies, right.
So as a potential fit.
Okay, so it sounds to me like the best.
Sorry, there was a point there we're doing retainer work where I'm leaning into my C suite CEO positioning, CMO positioning ability and wrapping the insight.
So we have a retainer of 20, $25,000 a month plus the research.
Okay, got you.
So it seems to me like the best option for you guys would possibly be to see if you can find somebody to acquire the company.

Because you were talking about like an Aqua Higher scenario and you've, you've spoken to another or a couple of potential buyers, PR companies, etc, so you, I mean you could get, you could try and get a partner to merge with.
That's one way to go down the track.
And that's something that we've just started recently because there are lots of agency owners like yourself who would kind of get stuck around that million mark.
Sometimes they go a bit over, but you know, it's kind of a roller coaster from year to year.

And just being able to sort of get rid of duplication within each other's businesses and have more founders involved would just really strengthen the business overall, but also adds a huge amount of value as well, adding two businesses together.
So if you did want to exit in three years, the businesses would just be worth more.
You're bigger, there's more people, there's more management, et cetera.
So that's one route is either to go down that route where we try and find you a partner, a market as a merge opportunity, which means that nobody needs to spend money.

It purely is, let's find some chemistry with some other founders and basically you're just building a, a cap table with equity, you know, and swapping equity into a holding company or just merging the two businesses.
So that's, that's definitely an option.
Or the other one is, is to put the business up for sale and find a larger company that is happy to, you know, pay, pay some money up front.
You get salaries that way and you would get some kind of earn out over a two or three year period to get the rest of them.

Yes, the preferred option, I'm glad that you mentioned it, is option one because we, you know, we're not, we're not spring chickens, but we're going to be working for a while saying, and I don't want to be squeezed out of, of a, you know, a PE scenario.
I've heard too many horror stories there.
And then, you know, have what, you know, then what do you.
Do you have to go get a job or not?
But you know, I don't think that the point is it would be great to take what we've built and put it with somebody else where one plus one equals three.
That's what we've been trying to do on our own, just through people we know.
But that's not the way to do that.
Right?
Yeah.
Well, you need lots of options.
You've got to kiss a lot of frogs.
I mean, that's the way to do it.
So there's a few ways we can do this.
Basically there's a more passive route where we put you up on the site and obviously we've got traffic coming to the site all the time.
We market to our 20,000 people on the mailing list.

So it's likely we will get a few matches that way or we can actually market the opportunity as well, not just to our mailing list, but also we actually go out and look for somebody that's likely to be a match.

So for instance, if you thought it was PR firms or there was a particular B2B type of agency that we could go out and look for, we would find all of those types of businesses that are a similar size size and then market the opportunity to match with you in that way.
And then it's kind of, it is a bit more like a dating service.
So we're setting you up, you're basically having chemistry calls with those founders on the understanding that they are also interested in the idea of a merger and not acquiring the company.
Although potentially a buyer situation could come up out of those conversations.
We, we are finding that a lot of companies would merge rather than, you know, buy because obviously it involves more risk to do that.
So.

Yeah, and I mean from your professional opinion based off of what Julie said, I mean we are offering consulting services, but we do use AI in a very responsible way that has Human input, which I would imagine would be appealing to someone who doesn't want to build their own tech but is ultimately going to have to have some tech at some point.
So curious.
100% I agree.

So the amount of times that we have had buy side mandates and we have gone out and you know, found maybe 50 companies like yours that do this, this kind of stuff and it's, we've never closed the deal on, on these type of things because you guys are unicorns.
You know, it's so difficult to find good businesses and also just to get a match, you know, on both sides.
You know, the buyer wants to.
Is, am I, am I frozen or is it.
No, I think I can hear you.
I just can't hear.
Andy, Andy, you're frozen for some reason.
You can hear us.
Have I paused?
Yeah, now we can hear you.
Sorry.
I've got a satellite dish in on the side of a hill, so sometimes it gets blocked by a tree.
So basically what I'm saying is, you know, we, we've, we've tried to get deals done with companies like yours and for, for our buyer buy side clients.
Usually we're buying like four or five different agencies, but they always say can we get some measurement in there as well?
But it's just so difficult to get high quality businesses that want to sell and find those, those, you know, founders that are looking for what you're looking for.
So what I would say is that you are, you know, an attractive type of marketing firm to, to exist.
You know, we can't find enough of you basically.
So that's refreshing to hear.
I see.
I knew you were going to be someone I liked.
Clever, attractive.
That's good.
Yeah.
I mean, listen, we, we, I mean, I do think putting, putting aside whatever personal feelings, I mean, we have really cool tech.
It works.
It's been proven with Fortune 500 brands.
We just need, we're tired of having the onus of having to go get the leads ourselves and quite frankly we're not ready to sell.
And we think that we could be better with a partner to your point, who wants to exit with us not now, but in three to five years.
Yeah.
Okay.
So.
So really the ball's in your court to sort of decide what level of investment and time you're looking to, to put into the process.
Like I say, it's very easy to sign up onto the site.
It's $290 a month and you can just sit there as a listing.
Obviously there's traffic coming to the site.
We're marketing all the time or we can actively go out and try and find a match.

And like I said, we're not just reliant then on, on our own mailing list to, to market the opportunity, but we actually build a bespoke list of potential matches and go out and pitch the opportunity to those agencies.
So that could be more exciting.
It's more likely that we're going to get a match.
The idea would be that we spend the next sort of three to six months doing that and trying to find.
How does that work monetarily?
Yeah.
So that's at the moment because we are, we're building this service out.
There's two ways to go and I would say the, the, there's a 4800amonth and that usually is for six months.
And that's really aimed at companies that are over 5 million, you know, 5 to 10 million in revenue.
So I'd say that the, the, the best opportunity is the $2800.
It's a one off fee.
It's targeted at companies like yourselves so that we can run this for something like three to six months.
That's basically the idea.
We go out, we build the list, we market to those companies and we book them into your calendar.
As soon as we've got leads, we're referring them to you, making sure that you like them, get them signed into an NDA and then we give them the pitch.
This is who it is.
And get you set up in a meeting and see if there's, there's chemistry.
Basically we can get a deal done.
That's, that's the idea.
And, and I would assume you there's a success fee for you.
Not that I don't think you should have one.
I'm just curious what it is.
We're not doing success fees on mergers because there is nothing for, for us to take.
There's no, there's not like a reasonable fee that we can take.
We're literally offering this service for a one off fee.
Yeah, it's, it's pretty much a no brainer.
Yeah, it is a no brainer.
And then in just in talking to us and, and thinking, I mean it sounds like it's a new thing of the conversion rate that you've seen or that you're hoping for in these kind of scenarios.
I mean what, what would be your best guess in, in, in finding?
So, so usually I would say roughly about a third of, of our deals close.
Actually the industry standard is 1 in 10.
So I would say it's going to be along those lines.
We, we're really good at what we do and that's contacting agencies and pitching an opportunity.
Then it really just does fall on the founders from both sides whether a deal can get done and whether everybody, you know, continue to put enough effort in to get it over the line.
So, but we're going to, you know, this is, it's not just a fire and forget process.
We are, we're going to, you know, nurture the whole process on both sides to get a deal done and get a merger to happen.
That's our intention.
So I would, you know, at this point, I don't know, but it is, it is roughly around one in three.
But you really have to have effort on both sides and it's not, you know, it's not a quick fix.
It's something that does take a fair bit of work to get over the line.
So.
Well, that's something that we're not afraid of and you know, it's happy to do the work to, to you know, grow what we have.
And I'm just out of curiosity, I mean I told you what our feeling is about roll ups, but is there something that I'm missing that maybe I should be.
We should be thinking about in terms.
Of running a roll up.
Obviously there's expense in building a roll up.

The roll ups that we're currently doing, we're looking for businesses with over $1 million EBITDA because we're looking to leverage some of the economics that change when you get about 5,5 million EBITDA in terms of roll up.

Obviously it is all about multiple arbitrage and that's the best thing for every agency owner because the, the real issue is that when you come to sell, you're getting those single low digit multiples for your business.
And really what a roll up does is it solves that problem.
So whether you are part of somebody else's roll up or your own is going to change a lot of variables as to how you cash out.

And when you cash out, most roll ups, they would be run by like a private equity or they would run by a larger agency and they would give a certain amount of cash, like 50 of the cash to each business that comes in and then roll some equity.
So they would be in control of, of it and they would take the biggest upside of on those types of deals.
Okay, well I appreciate you educating us.
You know, as I said, my, obviously I have to speak to Julie, but my instinct is the first option because that's what instinctually we were trying to do on our own.
And it's nice to know that you're doing that now.
Seems like a very fair and equitable model that you've built.
Would certainly love to look at the site.
I didn't.
What is the site?
Because I honestly didn't.
It's Agencies co.
I need to jump on another call.
Thank you.
But I'm going to give you the link here, so if you can see it popping up, because that's the.
That's the actual merge page.
So if you click it, it should take you onto the merge landing page.
So basically we talked about the Merge Match and Merge Merge Pro, and I think the Merge Pro is the best one in this instance.
It would allow us to build that bespoke list of potential agency matches.
Okay, we'll be in touch.
We really appreciate it.
I'll put it in an email as well.
I'll put in an email and then hopefully we can get.
We can get started in the next week or two.
That's great.
Thanks, Andy.
All right, Lovely to meet you both.
Enjoy the rest of your day.

summary.overview: In the recent exploratory call between Billee Howard of Brand Throw and Andy Day from Capital A, the discussion centered on Brand Throw's innovative AI-driven approach to emotional analysis in marketing and the potential for strategic collaboration. Both parties introduced their backgrounds, with Andy highlighting Capital A's focus on M&A in the agency space, while Billee shared insights into Brand Throw's recent performance, including completing 15 proof of concepts in 2023 and generating $1.3M in revenue. Key topics included potential paths for Brand Throw, such as exploring merger opportunities or an outright sale, with Billee expressing a preference for a merger. Andy proposed their advisory services, detailing options for both passive and active engagement, while both expressed a commitment to continue discussions in the coming weeks. Action items were assigned, including follow-up communications regarding merger possibilities and a review of the relevant agency resources.
summary.short_summary: In a recent exploratory call, Billee Howard from Brand Throw and Andy Day from Capital A discussed the innovative AI-driven emotional analysis that Brand Throw employs in marketing. Billee highlighted Brand Throw's 2023 achievements, including 15 proof of concepts and generating $1.3M in revenue, while also noting challenges such as an investor backing out. The conversation included potential paths for Brand Throw, with a preference for mergers over outright sales. Andy detailed Capital A's advisory services, including passive and active engagement options, as they both expressed commitment to further discussions about merger possibilities.
